registryEvidence.locality: The municipal transparency portal identifies Puerto Vallarta Sub Dirección de Catastro, its responsible areas, address, telephone extensions, and cadastral procedures; Jalisco Catastro publishes the statewide eCarto cartography portal.
registryEvidence.scopeNote: This evidences a local municipal cadastral custodian and a state public cartographic viewer, not citywide public parcel-data coverage or legal-survey completeness.

parcelDiscovery.nativeIdentityObserved: eCarto UTFGrid ecarto_id values for manzana/redvial map features only; no parcel identity was observed.
parcelDiscovery.crs: Web map coordinates are served for a Leaflet map; the inspected configuration did not expose a parcel geometry CRS or parcel feature schema.
parcelDiscovery.boundedResponse: The exact WUP point was converted only for tile addressing, without shifting the point. At zoom 18, the public UTFGrid tile returned map-feature metadata including layer=manzana/ecarto_id=207151 and nearby manzana/redvial records; it returned no parcel polygon and no safe parcel ID+geometry response.
parcelDiscovery.note: The current map configuration exposes Cartografía Estatal and Jalisco-IIEGJ tile layers, with UTFGrid interaction. Its visible info-window template for the cartographic layer references cuenta, which was not requested or retained because cadastral account fields are outside the safe allowlist. No polygon GeoJSON was retained.

The public eCarto map is a first-party statewide cartographic viewer, but the inspected current configuration exposed raster/vector tile and UTFGrid map features rather than parcel polygons with a safe native parcel identity.
The municipal pages evidence a cadastral custodian and request-based cadastral information services; they do not establish anonymous public parcel geometry access or citywide coverage.
No owner, address, contact, titleholder, personal, tax, account, certificate, or other unsafe fields were requested or retained.
